scope.window: ONE DAY, 20251204, bounded to at most 3 hours
scope.coins: every coin present in the walked hours; the hygiene legs count dropped and malformed records and are not cut by coin

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

checks.name: markout_formula_byte_identical
checks.assumption: ks2_persistence_10day.py carries a DUPLICATED (not imported) copy of the signed-markout formula identical to build_quickwin_markouts.py.
checks.method: Textually grepped the markout RHS 'taker_dir.astype(np.float64) * (ref - taker_px) / taker_px * 1e4' in both files and compared the whitespace-normalised line sets.
checks.note: markout RHS expression is byte-identical wherever it appears in both parser copies (ks2 keeps an extra compute_markout60 with the same RHS; build keeps a docstring - neither changes the arithmetic).

checks.name: searchsorted_join_byte_identical
checks.assumption: the as-of (last-at-or-before) join 'np.searchsorted(print_ts, query_ns, side="right") - 1' is duplicated identically in both parser copies.
checks.method: Textually grepped the searchsorted line in both files and compared the whitespace-normalised line sets; backstopped by comparing the full normalised source of price_at + compute_markouts_all.
checks.note: as-of join + price_at + compute_markouts_all are byte-identical across the two copies.

checks.name: parse_day_codeonly_diff
checks.assumption: build_quickwin_markouts.parse_day is 'copied verbatim' into ks2_persistence_10day.parse_day (per the docstring).
checks.method: Stripped docstrings/comments/blanks from BOTH parse_day sources and diffed code-line sets; asserted the load-bearing CORE anchors (VWAP print-path accumulation, crossed=true collapse, searchsorted join) are present in both, and allow-listed the one known benign divergence (ks2 drops the crossed=false maker branch + the extra retained taker fields). Any line outside the allow-list is flagged as a NEW divergence.
checks.note: parse_day is NOT verbatim-identical (build 146 code-lines vs ks2 92), but the ONLY divergence is the allow-listed benign one: ks2 omits the crossed=false maker branch + dominant-maker resolution and the extra retained fields (is_open/start_pos/side_b/closed_pnl/dir_code). The shared core - per-hash VWAP print-path accumulation, the crossed=true taker collapse and the markout/as-of-join - is identical.

checks.name: crossed_silent_drop_fraction
checks.assumption: Every raw fill is routed to either the taker branch (crossed is True) or the maker branch (crossed is False); a fill with crossed absent/None contributes to NEITHER and is silently dropped from counterparty resolution.
checks.method: Re-walked 3 hour(s) of 20251204 (BTC+ETH) at the raw event level, mirroring parse_day's loop and the same coin / ZERO_HASH / None-hash guards; counted fills by crossed routing as a fraction of raw fills.
checks.note: crossed-absent fraction 0.00e+00 (+other 0.00e+00) is negligible: effectively no fill is silently dropped on the crossed routing.

checks.name: size_nonpositive_fraction
checks.assumption: sz is read as float(f['sz']) unconditionally and is assumed strictly positive (no sz<=0 fills entering the VWAP / size-weighting).
checks.method: On the same raw re-walk, counted fills with sz<=0 and fills where px/sz are not float-parseable, as fractions of raw fills.
checks.note: no non-positive or unparseable sizes in the sample - the VWAP / size-weighting inputs are clean.

checks.name: maker_none_rate
checks.assumption: Most taker (hash,taker) sweeps have a crossed=false leg sharing the hash, so maker_id is resolved (maker_id == -1 only rarely). The FINAL artifacts show maker_id==-1 at 0.0.
checks.method: On the same raw re-walk, measured the fraction of distinct (hash,taker) takers with NO crossed=false leg sharing the hash within the walked window (these become maker_id == -1).

observed.note_window: windowed to the walked hours; a maker leg in an un-walked hour of the same hash would lower this rate, so this is an UPPER bound on the true per-day rate.

checks.note: maker-None rate 0.000 (upper bound on a 3-hour window) is small: maker resolution covers ~all taker sweeps, consistent with the 0.0 maker_id==-1 rate in the final npz.

note: BOTH halves ran and passed: load-bearing parser lines are identical (benign allow-listed parse_day divergence aside) AND the raw re-walk found negligible silent-drop / sz<=0.
